title: add-slo-weighted-synthetic-probe-gate-and-traffic-sensitive-thresholding
author: Asha Gupta
description: Summary: Adds an SLO-weighted synthetic probing subsystem plus a traffic-sensitive rollout gate that pauses traffic shifts when estimated customer-impact cost exceeds a configurable budget. Motivation: existing canary detectors are excellent at flagging distributional regressions but lack a synthesized customer-impact signal for gradual SLO regressions and lack a simple budget-aware throttle mechanism for rollouts. This PR implements a lightweight probe coordinator that runs shot-noise controlled synthetic probes across zones and model variants, computes an SLO-weighted impact score (latency breach severity * user-surface weight), and surfaces a single gate decision to the rollout controller. Implementation notes: 1) services/canary/probe_coordinator.py: new coordinator that schedules synthetic probes with jittered cadence, records KV-cache warmness tags, and exposes a small JSON metrics endpoint for the gate. 2) services/canary/gate_controller.go: evaluates an economic impact score using configurable SLO weights per route and a sliding window that is traffic-aware (sensitivity scales down under low traffic to avoid false positives). 3) pkg/observability/metrics.yaml: adds gauge and histogram metrics for probe latency, breach-rate, and computed impact_score. 4) infra/terraform/modules/canary/main.tf: optional probe instances as spot-backed tasks with autoscale bounds. 5) tests/canary/integration/test_slo_gate.py and unit tests added for edge cases (cold KV cache and partial regional degradation). Rollout & migration: default is off. Console feature flag and route-level config added so teams can enable probe-gate per rollout; default gate thresholds are conservative. We validated in perf-lab with synthetic traffic and in one customer sandbox with zero user-visible regressions. Backwards compatibility: the gate is a best-effort hook — absence of the probe subsystem falls back to existing canary detectors. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-3456 - [x] unit tests for coordinator scheduling and gate math - [x] integration tests against canary-simulator - [x] instrumentation (traces + metrics) - [x] rollout plan and sticky flag gating - [x] docs: ops runbook and console controls Added docs: docs/ops/canary-runbook.md includes emergency bypass and troubleshooting steps. Performance: probes run at <1% of a single p50 CPU on probe instances when scaled to our standard canary fleet. Security & cost: probe traffic uses internal certs and sandboxed egress; default infra uses spot capacity to limit cost. Review conversation (high level): Miguel: "Can the impact score be gamed by probe cadence?" Author: "We normalize by observed request rate and include an outlier cap; tests added." Lena: "Add explicit behavior when region is partial-down; we should prefer fallback instead of full halt." Author: "Added regional weighting and fallback policy in gate_controller.go." Owen: "CI flake on test_slo_gate sometimes; looks like race on metrics export." Author: "Added deterministic seeding and a short test-only sleep to stabilize." CI: all checks passed after two reruns (unit, integration in perf-lab, lint). Merge: squashed and merged to main; merged_at=2025-11-19. Impact & follow-ups: - Follow-up to add adaptive probe cadence learning based on workload (ENG-3610). - Ops: recommend adding an alert for sustained impact_score > 0.5 for 10m with auto-revert playbook. Related: augments existing canary detectors by providing a customer-impact lens and an economic throttle to rollout controllers.

release_notes: Adds an optional SLO-weighted synthetic probe subsystem and a traffic-sensitive rollout gate to prevent high-impact regressions during rollouts. Default disabled; enable per-route via console flag. See ops runbook for emergency bypass.
